founders.name: Angela Landrith
founders.title: Co-Founder & CEO
bio: Angela brings twenty-two years of corporate product management experience across mortgage, financial services, and technology — and the kind of pattern recognition that comes from watching the same gap appear across every industry she worked in: capable people, blocked by a system that required experience to get experience.
She left corporate eighteen months ago to commit to Transition Trails full-time. The nonprofit was already running alongside her day job. Once she chose, she chose fully.

founders.name: Kim Barnes
founders.title: Co-Founder & COO
bio: Kim is the person who figures out how the thing actually gets built. Where Angela sees the vision, Kim sees the system required to deliver it — the architecture, the process, the nonprofit technology stack that makes the model scalable.
She has been part of Transition Trails from the beginning, working alongside Angela through every iteration of what the programs needed to be before they were ready for learners.

founders.name: Hugh Richardson
founders.title: Co-Founder & CTO · Solutions Architect
bio: Hugh is the proof of concept. The first CLYLP project — the one that became the blueprint for Guided Trail — was his. He learned while doing, delivered real work for a real client, and came out the other side with the experience that the job market had been telling him he needed to get first.
That experience is now what he helps every Guided Trail learner build. He knows exactly what it costs to break in because he paid it himself.

founders.name: Kel Landrith
founders.title: Co-Founder & Finance Director
bio: Kel joined Transition Trails to build the foundation that lets everything else stand. When it came time to formalize the nonprofit — navigate the IRS, establish the books, set up the financial infrastructure — Kel brought the nonprofit accounting and compliance experience to do it right.
He is not a Salesforce practitioner. He is the reason the organization can operate with the integrity that grant funders and partners expect.
